headline: New law lets the Capitol Police Board allow officers to keep working until as late as age 62, up from 60.
what_it_does: Capitol Police officers generally must retire at age 57, or once they finish 20 years of service if they are already older than 57. Before this law, the Capitol Police Board could grant a waiver letting an officer work until age 60. This law lets the board set a retirement age anywhere from 57 to 62 when it decides doing so is in the public interest.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. Capitol Police
who_it_affects.how: Officers who receive a waiver from the board may be allowed to keep working up to age 62 instead of a maximum of 60.
The board gains the power to grant waivers setting a retirement age anywhere between 57 and 62.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 29, 2026; the summary does not give a separate start date.
